title: TradeAgreement
description:
A seller issued sales contract, also called a sale confirmation.
The buyer issued mirror of this document is {@link IPurchaseOrder}; the
seller assigns the contract number, so `sellerReference` is mandatory here.
See docs/model-guide.md §2.3.

sellerReference.description: A seller reference, expressed as text, for this header trade agreement.

issueDateTime.description: The date the document was issued.

saleDate.description:
The date the sale was concluded, as stated in the confirmation sentence.
Distinct from `issueDateTime`: a confirmation can be written up after the
sale is struck.

buyerParty.description: The buyer party for this sales contract.

sellerParty.description: The seller party for this sales contract.

includedSupplyChainTradeLineItem.description:
A contracted lot. Optional: a single lot contract states quantity,
quality and price at header level and has no line breakdown.

applicableDeliveryTerms.description:
The delivery terms: the Incoterm and its named place, plus the weight
basis, tolerance and tare rules as verbatim text.

applicableLocation.description:
A place named by this contract, such as the destination. Discriminate
with `locationFunctionTypeCode`.

salesConditionsDocument.description: Conditions the contract is subject to, in `processCondition`.

contractDocument.description: A document whose terms govern this contract.

includedNote.description:
Contractual prose with no typed UN/CEFACT slot, discriminated by
`subject`. See {@link IPurchaseOrder.includedNote}.

Date.title: Date
Date.description:
A date carried by a trade document.
`DateValue` is an unconstrained string for now, so it accepts the document's
own wording as well as a normalised form. No `format` is asserted until the
representation is settled.

DateValue.description: The date, as printed on the document or normalised.

TradeParty.title: TradeParty
TradeParty.description:
A party taking a role in a trade document, such as the buyer or the seller.
Only the name is mandatory: sample documents identify counterparties by name
alone, so requiring an address would reject a real document. The address,
role codes, identifiers and contacts are all inherited and optional.

name.description: A name, expressed as text, for this trade party.

brandName.description: A brand name, expressed as text, for this trade party.

postalAddress.description: The postal address for this trade party.

DeliveryTerms.title: DeliveryTerms
DeliveryTerms.description:
The delivery terms of a trade document. The Incoterm goes in
`deliveryTermsDeliveryTypeCode` and its named place in `relevantLocation`;
weight basis, tolerance and tare rules have no typed slot and go verbatim in
`description`.

PaymentTerms.title: PaymentTerms
PaymentTerms.description:
The terms of payment agreed for a trade document. Carry the verbatim text in
`description` and the code list value in `paymentTermsTypeCode`.

description.description: A textual description of these trade payment terms.
